# Results — Study 210 (Crypto-Trend) on real BTC-USD daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The 200-day SMA timing
rule applied to BTC-USD daily closes: hold Bitcoin when price is above SMA(200), hold
cash (4%/yr flat proxy) otherwise. Binary in/out, 10 bps one-way cost. Compared against
buy-and-hold BTC and a random-timing control (same in-market fraction, random days).
All figures annualised on 365 days/year (crypto never closes). As-of **2026-06-15**.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | n | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| BTC-USD | 2014-09-17 → 2026-06-15 | 4,290 | `fcd9bda77d20` |

## The three-arm comparison

In-market fraction (SMA rule): **58.6%**  |  Total SMA switches: **74** (~6.7/yr)

| Arm | CAGR | Sharpe | Vol | MaxDD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Buy-and-hold BTC** | **+52.77%** | **+0.632** | 67.09% | **−83.40%** |
| **SMA(200) timing** | **+58.82%** | **+0.902** | 51.28% | **−70.10%** |
| **Random timing (null)** | +11.01% | +0.209 | 50.08% | −83.28% |

**Sharpe diff t-stat (SMA timing vs buy-and-hold): +0.32** — directional but not certified (|t| < 2).

**Sharpe diff t-stat (SMA timing vs random timing): +2.63** — above the inference bar (|t| ≥ 2). Timing skill confirmed.

**Drawdown improvement (timing vs BH): +13.3 percentage points.**

Key observations:
- The SMA rule beats buy-and-hold on BOTH Sharpe and CAGR on this tape — unlike the equity
  case (Study 110) where timing costs some return. This reflects BTC's especially deep bear
  markets and the SMA's ability to sidestep large portions of 2018 and 2022.
- The random-timing control has nearly the same drawdown as buy-and-hold (−83.28% vs −83.40%),
  confirming that the SMA's −70.10% drawdown comes from identifying the *right* days to be out,
  not just from reduced exposure. This is the study's key test.
- The Sharpe improvement vs buy-and-hold alone (*t* = +0.32) is not statistically certified —
  the 11-year history with only 74 switches is too short for high-power inference.

## Cost sweep (SMA timing, varying one-way bps)

| One-way cost | Sharpe | MaxDD | CAGR |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | +0.914 | −69.90% | +59.83% |
| 1.0 bps | +0.913 | −69.91% | +59.73% |
| 5.0 bps | +0.908 | −70.00% | +59.32% |
| **10.0 bps (base)** | **+0.902** | **−70.10%** | **+58.82%** |
| 25.0 bps | +0.884 | −70.41% | +57.33% |
| 50.0 bps | +0.853 | −70.93% | +54.87% |

The Sharpe remains above buy-and-hold (+0.632) even at 50 bps one-way. With ~7 switches/year,
costs are almost irrelevant to the strategy's viability.

## Sub-era breakdown (SMA timing vs buy-and-hold)

| Era | BH Sharpe | BH MaxDD | SMA Sharpe | SMA MaxDD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2014-2017 (first bull run) | +1.43 | −59.1% | +1.85 | −35.5% |
| 2018-2020 (bear market + recovery) | +0.33 | −81.5% | +1.22 | −49.7% |
| 2021-2022 (choppy top + crash) | −0.39 | −76.6% | −0.65 | −36.7% |
| 2023-2026 (new cycle) | +0.85 | −51.2% | +0.63 | −31.8% |

Key takeaway: the rule is strongly regime-dependent. It shines in 2018-2020 (sustained bear
market — the SMA correctly identified and avoided the crash). In 2021-2022, the choppy Bitcoin
top generated whipsaws that hurt the strategy's Sharpe even while still reducing drawdown
(−36.7% vs −76.6% for BH). In the 2023-2026 bull market it underperformed BH on Sharpe.

## Synthetic positive control

On a BTC-calibrated two-state Markov synthetic tape (signal_strength=1.0), the SMA(200)
rule substantially reduces drawdown vs buy-and-hold and beats the random-timing control.
On a flat-vol null tape (signal_strength=0.0), it adds no reliable advantage. This confirms
the machinery is correct and the real-tape benefit comes from real regime structure.

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** Sharpe +0.902 vs BH +0.632; max DD −70.10% vs BH −83.40% (+13.3 pp).
  Timing vs random control: *t* = +2.63 (above the inference bar). Timing vs BH: *t* = +0.32
  (directional, not certified on this 11-year tape). The drawdown protection is confirmed as
  genuine timing skill.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** ~7 switches/yr; cost-insensitive down to 50 bps one-way. Key
  fragilities: (1) 11-year history (74 switches) gives limited statistical power; (2) strong
  regime-dependence (whipsaws in 2021-2022); (3) behavioral challenge of sitting in cash for
  months during BTC bull markets.
- **Drawdown shield? — CONFIRMED.** Vol falls from 67.09% to 51.28%; max DD cut from −83.40%
  to −70.10%. The random-timing control cannot replicate this (−83.28%), confirming genuine
  timing skill in identifying BTC bear-market regimes.
